hint.label: Skill

atoms.text:
Virginia Woolf's novel tells the story of Orlando, who starts out as an aristocratic man and turns into a woman halfway through. Orlando pursues many romantic interests, both as a man and woman, many of whom do not conform to traditional gender roles either. She marries a man named Shel, who used to be a woman. Both he and Orlando exhibit a mix of stereotypically male as well as female traits.
As Orlando contemplates her gender throughout the book, she finally realises that her identity is too complex to be put in terms of either “male” or “female”.

atoms.a: Which terms could be used to describe Orlando and Shel? (Multiple may apply.)
Orlando's love interests include both men and women, as well as gender nonconforming people. How could we describe her sexual orientation?

instruction.text: Decide whether the statements are true or false.

atoms.a: Orlando shows that sexual and gender identity are fluid and can change throughout one's life.
Orlando and Shel's gender identities match their original biological sexes.
Orlando and Shel conform to society's expectations of men and women.
Orlando identifies with a binary gender identity.

hint.label: Vocabulary

atoms.text:
[Orlando] remembered how, as a young man, she had insisted that women must be obedient, chaste, scented and exquisitely apparelled. “Now I shall have to pay in my own person for those desires [...] There's the hairdressing,” she thought, “that alone will take an hour of my morning; there's the looking glass, another hour; there's staying and laying; there's washing and powdering [...]”
[S]he was horrified to perceive how low of an opinion she was forming of the other sex, the manly, to which it had once been her pride to belong. [...]
[S]he was censuring both sexes equally, as if she belonged to neither; and indeed, for the time being, she seemed to vacillate; she was a man; she was a woman; she knew the secrets, shared the weaknesses of each. [...] Thus it is no great wonder, as she pitted one sex against the other, [...] [she] was not sure to which she belonged.

atoms.b: Orlando ((++regrets enjoys)) how she acted when she was a man, but she also ((appreciates ++does_not_appreciate)) the beauty routines women are expected to go through daily.

Forced to confront what it is like to live as a woman, Orlando feels ((++restricted freed happy)) by the expectations ((++society she nobody)) places onto her. Conforming to traditional ((++gender_roles biological_sex same-sex)) frustrates her and she desires to break free from them entirely.
